limits.why: the kernel's command catalog takes only names matching [A-Za-z0-9._+-], so '[' is not found (bash's builtin covers shells); close the kernel range at the release with the fix

before 1.86.0 the page has no kernel.chmod, so the harness writes the shims straight to OPFS with the default 0644 instead of their tarball 0755, and since 1.78.0 the x bit is checked on exec: i's exec of ${0%/*}/npm by path is refused. From 1.86.0 run.mjs stamps the tarball modes (slicc-kernel#495 for the kernel side)
5.3.0-17's kill(getpid(), sig) exits 128+n in the program, so the kernel sees status 143 and no signal (slicc-kernel#422); 5.3.0-18's shim sends it to the kernel (NEGATIVE.md)
the spec checks bzip2recover-llu.patch, new in 1.0.8-2; 1.0.8-1 prints 'I/O error reading data.bz2' (NEGATIVE.md)

limits.case: root: tar -x keeps owners and modes
limits.why: 1.35.0-4 links the slicc shims from before process credentials, so root's tar -x acts as a non-root user and drops owners and setuid/setgid; 1.35.0-5 keeps them (NEGATIVE.md)
the destination's top directory loses its mtime after rsync -a, so the re-run itemizes '.d..t...... ./'; fixed by slicc-kernel#467 in 1.73.3

limits.case: installed with the tarball's modes: 644 \S+/bin/coreutils|bin/coreutils by path as cone under users enforce: rc=126
limits.why: 9.12.0-5 ships bin/coreutils (the glue) 0644, so with the tarball's modes (slicc-kernel >= 1.86.0) cone can't run it by path under enforce (126); 9.12.0-6 ships it 0755. Kernels before 1.86.0 have no kernel.chmod, so the harness leaves bin/ at the default 0755 and the reference passes

limits.case: installed with the tarball's modes: 644 \S+/bin/tar|bin/tar by path as cone under users enforce:[\s\S]*rc=126
limits.why: 1.35.0-5 ships bin/tar (the glue) 0644, so with the tarball's modes (slicc-kernel >= 1.86.0) cone can't run it by path under enforce (126); 1.35.0-6 ships it 0755. Kernels before 1.86.0 have no kernel.chmod, so the harness leaves bin/ at the default 0755 and the reference passes

5.42.0-11 ships bin/perl.wasm 0644, so with the tarball's modes (slicc-kernel >= 1.86.0) the spec sees 644; 5.42.0-12 ships it 0755. Kernels before 1.86.0 have no kernel.chmod, so the harness leaves bin/ at the default 0755 and the reference passes. Lapses when bios pins perl -12

limits.case: select\.poll with an events-0 fd: |register twice must be EEXIST: |unregister of an unregistered fd must be ENOENT:
limits.why: 3.14.2-19 and older link wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-28 or older (bios's catalog pins -18, on -27). That libc's poll() refuses an fd with events 0 (ENOSYS) before it reaches the kernel, and its epoll_ctl passes Linux's ADD (1) untranslated, which the kernel's dual numbering reads as add-or-modify: register twice gives 0, and so does unregister again (slicc-kernel#684 drops the dual numbering). 3.14.2-20 is on sysroot -29 (homescoop#443) and passes
up to 5.0.1-10 screen -v prints the build day (BUILD_DATE without SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH); 5.0.1-11 pins it to source.epoch and is byte-reproducible (#653, NEGATIVE.md). bios's catalog pins -10

limits.case: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES\.md is installed|wasi-libc \(wasi-sdk-31|Cannot read properties of null
limits.why: cert/notices.mjs (2.5.15-4, #550) checks the wasi-libc heading names wasi-sdk-33: 2.5.15-3 says wasi-sdk-31 and 2.5.15-2, which bios's catalog pins, ships no THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md (the spec then reads null)
12.9.1-8 and older were built from the published pnpm.wasm with build paths in it; 12.9.1-9 builds from source without them, which install.mjs checks (an old catalog pin, not a regression)
symloop.mjs checks 39, 40 and 41 symlink follows; Emscripten's FS.lookupPath gave ELOOP at 40 until scripts/emsdk-patches/libfs-symloop.patch, first in 9.12.0-8
checklist.mjs checks the 3.5.1 version line; 3.4.4-N prints 3.4.4 (the bios catalog's old pin)
daemon.mjs checks 'connect from localhost (127.0.0.1)' and hosts allow/deny by name, which need the shims' getnameinfo, rebuilt into 3.5.1-3
symlink-dest.mjs checks 3.5.x's destination-symlink hardening (#555), documented and certified from 3.5.1-2
launcher.mjs checks that RUBYLIB names only library directories that exist, from 3.4.11-14 (slicc-kernel#774's package side)
locks.mjs checks Fcntl::F_GETLK and record locks through slicc.fcntl_lock, from 3.4.11-14 on wasix-sysroot -30 (homescoop#552)
sysroot28.mjs expects the wasix-sysroot -30 toolchain record of 3.4.11-14; older builds name -27 or -28

concurrent.mjs tests the concurrent-import fixes of 2.4.9-8 (the fcntl dotlock, #874) and 2.4.9-9 (the complete-keybox create, #951). Before -9, gpg loses a different key, or fails a different lock assertion, in every run (the bios pin is 2.4.9-5), so any per-case limit keeps missing the next case by chance (#985, #1064). Every concurrent.mjs case is known below 2.4.9-9 except --check-trustdb, the engines floor and crashes (JS Type/Reference/Syntax/RangeError, wasm RuntimeError, unreachable, trap), which are still compared with the reference. 2.4.9-9 and later are held to the full spec, and the readers round to 2.4.9-10.

limits.case: readers round \d+:|doesn't share its inode number
limits.why: The readers round and the inode check test 2.4.9-10's fixes. Up to 2.4.9-8, readers can see a half-written keybox (the creation race fixed in -9, #951); up to 2.4.9-9, every update renames from one pubring.kbx.tmp, so readers can read another file's bytes on kernels before slicc-kernel#954's fix (1.123.1). The bios pin is 2.4.9-5, so these fail on any kernel. 2.4.9-10 and later are held to them.
